title: In Situ Mapping of the Mechanical Properties of Biofilms by Particle-tracking Microrheology
protocol: Inoculate 2 ml of appropriate growth medium from frozen bacterial culture for mucoid P. aeruginosa and its Δpel and Δpsl defective mutants.
Incubate the cultures overnight at 37 °C with shaking at 200 rpm.
Dilute overnight cultures to an OD600 of 0.40 using a spectrophotometer.
Assemble flow cell setup for biofilm cultivation.
Prepare sterile growth medium in 2 L or 5 L bottles, using minimal medium M9 supplemented with 0.04% glucose and 0.2% casamino acids for P. aeruginosa.
Aliquot fluorescent microspheres into microcentrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge the microsphere aliquots at 9,391.2 g for 5 min to pellet them.
Remove the supernatant from the centrifuged microspheres.
Resuspend pelleted microspheres in 1 ml of growth medium to remove sodium azide.
Disperse 120 µl of 1.0 µm diameter microspheres into 2 L of growth medium.
Disperse 15 µl of 0.5 µm diameter microspheres into 2 L of growth medium.
Disperse 0.96 µl of 0.2 µm diameter microspheres into 2 L of growth medium to give 2.18 × 10^6 microspheres/ml for each particle size.
Attach the medium bottle to the upstream of the flow cell and allow the growth medium to flow through the entire setup.
Stop the flow and inject diluted overnight cultures into the flow cell chambers.
Allow bacteria to attach to the coverslip substratum for 1 hour before continuing the flow of growth medium at a flow rate of approximately 5.5 × 10^-3 m/sec or 8 rpm with a peristaltic pump.
Add 200 µl of diluted overnight culture with particles to the chambers of 8 well slides.
Incubate at 37 °C under static conditions.
Replace spent growth medium daily with fresh growth medium containing particles if biofilm is grown for more than 1 day.
Switch off flow from peristaltic pump on days 3 and 5.
Bring the flow cell setup into the microscopy room.
Clamp tubing near the entrance and exit of the flow cell chambers to prevent drift.
Place the flow cell onto the microscope stage of an upright microscope.
Use fluorescent microscopy with a 40X oil objective to take videos of microsphere motion embedded in the biofilm at various locations on day 3 and day 5.
Take shorter videos with higher frame rate to investigate fast dynamics events (e.g., 1.5-3 min videos at 25-50 frames per second).
Take longer videos with lower frame rate to investigate slower dynamics events over longer time scales (e.g., 15-30 min videos at 2.5-5 frames/sec).
Obtain particle trajectories using TrackMate in Fiji (ImageJ).
Open the video with Fiji.
Under the Plugins menu, select Tracking and then TrackMate.
Check or adjust settings to match video parameters from step 2.4.
Select 'LoG detector' for particle detection.
Input particle diameter and threshold value (e.g., 1,000).
Preview particle detection by clicking on 'Preview'.
Adjust diameter and threshold values as necessary: increase the threshold if circles appear in empty space; reduce it if too few particles are detected.
Click next to complete particle detection without adjusting detected particles if satisfactory.
Select 'Simple LAP tracker' for tracking particles that rarely move out of focus.
Use suggested or low linking and gap-closing max distance values.
Click next to proceed.
Check that particle tracking is satisfactory by scrolling through the video.
Select 'Export tracks to xml file' from the drop down menu.
Choose a folder to save the exported track xml files.
Prepare Matlab to import particle trajectories by selecting File>Set Path... and adding the scripts folder available with the Fiji package.
Download and extract the @msdanalyzer folder in a directory that belongs to the Matlab path.
Start Matlab and initiate the analyzer by typing ma = msdanalyzer(2, 'um', 'sec').
Import particle trajectories by typing:
```matlab
[tracks, md] = importTrackMateTracks('FileName.xml', 'clipZ', 'scaleT')
Add imported tracks to ma:
```matlab
ma = ma.addAll(tracks)
Plot the trajectories onto a graph using:
```matlab
ma.plotTracks
ma.labelPlotTracks
Compute the mean squared displacements (MSDs) of the particles using:
```matlab
ma = ma.computeMSD
ma.msd
Plot the MSDs of each particle:
```matlab
figure
ma.plotMSD
Combine particle trajectories from other videos by repeating the import and processing steps.
Plot the ensemble mean or average over all curves:
```matlab
ma.plotMeanMSD
Change the y- and x-axis from linear to logarithmic scale.
Select the end of the curve using the brush tool.
Remove unbrushed regions by selecting 'Brushing' > 'Remove Unbrushed'.
Download Ezyfit from http://www.fast.u-psud.fr/ezyfit/.
Add Ezyfit to a folder belonging to the Matlab path.
Install the Ezyfit menu by typing efmenu install in the Matlab workspace.
Restart MATLAB with Ezyfit menu in the figure window.
Fit the MSD curves to the power law by selecting 'Show Fit' > 'Power' > 'a*x^n'.
Clear current particle trajectories and MSDs to calculate new particle MSDs at other locations or time.
Copy and paste mean MSD curves into one graph for comparison.
Select the curve.
Go to "Tools" to view data statistics such as median and range.
